situation.lean: Hold off: nothing fills, because credit stress still keeps even the first entry shut and the AI-earnings season came in mixed rather than weak. The chip-rule extension and the calm Fed and BoJ holds take policy and rates off the table for now, leaving credit and Oracle's debt as the bear case.
situation.slow: The grind is still credit: CCC spreads sit flat above the escalation line rather than easing, and Oracle keeps funding its data-center build at investment grade one notch above junk. A renewed widening or an Oracle cut to junk keeps every entry shut however the earnings read.
situation.fast: The gap risk sits in the tape: the market sold Alphabet and Amazon hard after they raised spend, so data-center capex is being priced as cost without return. NVDA's print is the next one that can turn that into a guide-cut story in a day.
situation.decides: The 11-10 affiliates-rule expiry no longer bites now that the suspension runs into January, and moves no slot. NVDA on 11-17 decides whether the AI anchors still guide up and holds the larger entries until it passes; the 12-09 Fed meeting with new dots and Broadcom's 12-10 print then test rates and AI-funding demand. Alphabet's, Meta's and Amazon's prints stay open until a first 2027 capex figure or a calmer tape settles them, most likely with the January reports.
situation.flips: A first 2027 capex number at or below +10 % from any hyperscaler, an NVDA guide below consensus, or an Oracle cut to junk moves the lean to bear. CCC turning back under the fizzle line with NVDA guiding up would move it toward fizzle.
